title: Sameer Joseph Francis Saldanha vs Shona Christable D'Sa Prabhu on 11 March, 2014

paragraphs.text:
1



 IN THE HIGH COURT OF KARNATAKA AT BANGALORE

 DATED THIS THE 11TH DAY OF MARCH 2014

 BEFORE
 THE HON'BLE MR.JUSTICE S. ABDUL NAZEER

 WRIT PETITION NO.12422 OF 2013 (GM-FC)

BETWEEN:

SAMEER JOSEPH FRANCIS SALDANHA
S/O. H.R.T.SALDANHA
AGED ABOUT 38 YEARS
R/AT NO.804, SYMPHONY APARTMENTS
STURROCK ROAD
FALNIR
MANGALORE .... PETITIONER

(BY SRI L. GOVINDRAJ, ADV.)


AND:

SHONA CHRISTABLE D'SA PRABHU
W/O. SAMEER JOSEPH FRANCIS SALDANHA
AGED ABOUT 36 YEARS
R/AT NO.20, REST HOUSE CRESCENT
BANGALORE - 560 001 ... RESPONDENT


(BY SRI. R.I.D'SA, ADV., FOR SMT.SUNITHA H SINGH, ADV.)


 THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 
 & 227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA, PRAYING TO
QUASH THE ORDER DATED 12.02.2013 MADE ON I.A.NO.6
IN M.C.NO.3610/2009 BY VI ADDITIONAL PRINCIPAL
 2



JUDGE, FAMILY COURT, BANGALORE (ANNEXURE-F) & IN
TURN ALLOW THE APPLICATION AND ETC.,

 THIS WRIT PETITION COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY
HEARING IN 'B' GROUP THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED
THE FOLLOWING:

 ORDER

This writ petition is directed against the order in

M.C.No.3610/2009 dated 12.02.2013, on the file of the

VI Additional Principal Judge, Family Court at

Bangalore, whereby the Court below has rejected the

application filed by the petitioner seeking amendment

of the petition.

2. The petitioner filed the above

case for dissolution of his marriage with

the respondent solemnized on 27.05.2000 under

 Section 10(x) of the Divorce Act, 1869 (for short

'the Act'). He filed the application - I.A.No.6 under

 Order 6 Rule 17 of Code of Civil Procedure , seeking

amendment of the petition. He wanted to
 3



introduce additional grounds under Section 10(i) 

and (ix) of the Act.

3. The application was opposed by the

respondent. As noticed above, the Court below has

rejected the application.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner would

contend that the petitioner wants to incorporate

additional plea available under Section 10(i) and (ix) of

the act. These developments have taken place

subsequent to the filing of the writ petition. The

amendment does not change the nature of the petition

for divorce nor the cause of action. No prejudice,

whatsoever will be caused to the respondent, if the

amendment application is allowed.

5. On the other hand, learned advocate

appearing for the respondent submits that in order to
 4



plead commission of adultery as a ground under

 Section 10(i) of the act, the petitioner has to make the

alleged adulterer as a co-respondent unless the

petitioner is excused from doing so. The petitioner has

not made an application seeking exemption from

impleading the adulterer as a party. He has also drawn

my attention to the proviso of Section 14 and submits

that the Court is not bound to pronounce decree for

dissolution of marriage, if it finds that the petitioner

has, during the marriage, been guilty of adultery, or of

having deserted or willfully separated himself or herself

from the other party before the adultery complained of,

and without reasonable excuse. In the instant case,

the petitioner is guilty of committing adultery. He has

deserted the respondent before the alleged adultery is

complained of. Therefore, no useful purpose will be
 5



served even if the amendment is allowed. He prays for

dismissal of the writ petition.

6. I have carefully considered the arguments

of the learned counsel made at the bar and perused

the materials placed on record.

7. As noticed above, the petition for divorce

was filed under Section 10(x) of the Act, on the ground

of cruelty. Now he wants to amend additional plea

under Section 10(i) and (ix) of the act, on the ground of

adultery and desertion. These two grounds are

pleaded on the basis of the subsequent developments,

which is clear from the affidavit filed in support of the

IA. No.6. If the application for amendment is allowed, it

does not change the nature of the petition nor the

cause of action. The respondent is at liberty to contest
 6



the matter by filing additional objections. Thus, no

prejudice whatsoever will be caused to the respondent.

8. Section 11 of the Act, states that on a

petition for dissolution of marriage presented by a

husband or wife on the ground of adultery, the

petitioner shall make the alleged adulterer or

adulteress a co-respondent, unless the petitioner is

excused by Court from so doing on any of the grounds

mentioned therein. In the instant case, the plea sought

to be raised has not become a part of the petition. If

the amendment is allowed then only the plea becomes

part of the petition. Thereafter, he has to take steps

either to implead the alleged adulterer or to seek

exemption from making the alleged adulterer a party.

I am not in agreement with the contention of the

learned counsel for the respondent that the application

for amendment has to be rejected at this stage itself.
 7

9. Whether, the petitioner is also guilty of

adultery or not has to be established by the

respondent by leading evidence. Similarly, whether,

the adultery complained of, is after desertion or

willfully separating himself from the respondent and

without reasonable excuses has also to be established

by leading evidence. These questions are on the merits

of the case. It is settled that merits of the case cannot

be gone into, while considering the application for

amendment of the pleadings.

10. I am of the view that the Court below is not

right in rejecting the application. Therefore, the order

of the Court below on IA.No.6 dated 12.02.2013 in

M.C.No.3610/2009 is hereby quashed. The application

I.A.No.6 is allowed. The petitioner is permitted to

amend the petition in M.C.No.3610/2009 within two
 8



weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

No costs.
